extraction.name: Science Question Answering (SCIENCE QA)
extraction.description: A large-scale multimodal multiple-choice science question dataset containing 21,208 examples with diverse science topics. Each example consists of a question, multiple choices, multimodal contexts (text and/or image), a correct answer, and annotations of lectures and explanations for the answers. The dataset is designed to evaluate multi-hop reasoning and interpretability in AI systems.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Tony Xia, Liang Qiu, Kai-Wei Chang, Song-Chun Zhu, Oyvind Tafjord, Peter Clark, Ashwin Kalyan
extraction.citeAs: Pan Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Tony Xia, Liang Qiu, Kai-Wei Chang, Song-Chun Zhu, Oyvind Tafjord, Peter Clark, Ashwin Kalyan. Leam to Explain: Multimodal Reasoning via Thought Chains for Science Question Answering. arXiv:2209.09513v2 [cs.CL] 17 Oct 2022
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected from open resources managed by IXL Learning, an online learning platform curated by experts in K-12 education. The questions align with California Common Core Content Standards. Invalid questions (e.g., single-choice, faulty data, duplicates) were manually removed. Answer options were shuffled to avoid specific patterns. Lectures and solutions were reformatted using semi-automated scripts to distinguish special structures like tables and lists. Data quality was ensured through a data exploration tool and manual revisions by experts.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Science questions sourced from open resources managed by IXL Learning, an online learning platform curated by experts in K-12 education. The dataset includes problems that align with California Common Core Content Standards.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Answer options were shuffled to ensure the choices do not follow any specific pattern. Lectures and solutions were reformatted using semi-automated scripts to distinguish special structures like tables and lists.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Invalid questions (e.g., single-choice, faulty data, duplicates) were manually removed. Lectures and solutions were reformatted to ensure special structures (e.g., tables, lists) are distinguishable from simple text passages. A data exploration tool was developed to review examples and manually revise incorrect annotations.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each example includes a lecture providing general knowledge and an explanation revealing specific reasons for the correct answer. The lecture and explanation are designed to mimic the multi-step reasoning process of humans when answering science questions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) for human evaluation of generated explanations and human performance studies. Semi-automated scripts and a data exploration tool were used for annotation and quality control.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human evaluations rated the relevance, correctness, and completeness of generated explanations. 65.2% of explanations generated by GPT-3 (CoT) met the gold standard of human evaluations. UnifiedQA BASE (CoT) generated the most similar explanations to the given ones based on automatic metrics.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Workers on Amazon Mechanical Turk who obtained a high school or higher degree and passed qualification examples. Each worker answered 10 test questions, with each question answered by three different workers. Compensation was $0.5 per HIT task, amounting to $6.0 per hour at a rate of 3 questions per minute.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: ViT (Visual Transformer) and GPT-2 for generating captions for images in the dataset. The captioning model was used to provide visual semantics for language models in VQA baselines.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is available for non-commercial research purposes under the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license. The copyright belongs to the original authors. The dataset and code are available at https://scienceqa.github.io. The dataset is maintained by the Allen Institute for AI (AI2).
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is designed to diagnose the multimodal understanding and multi-hop reasoning abilities of AI systems. It does not contain user usage data or personally sensitive information such as gender and race. The dataset adheres to the goal of AI for the common good, and any antisocial data points will be removed based on feedback.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is sourced from K-12 science curricula and may not fully represent real-world scientific reasoning. The image captions lack fine-grained semantics and may not work well for complex diagrams. Large language models may struggle with questions requiring complex or uncommon domain knowledge. The dataset may not generalize to all scientific domains or real-world scenarios.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. The dataset is intended for research in multimodal learning, multi-hop reasoning, and general artificial intelligence. It can also contribute to K-12 education applications such as tutoring systems. The dataset is designed to aid the development of AI systems capable of generating coherent chains of thought when answering science questions.
